# Complete Button & Interactive Element Audit

Unseen Jo — Discover Jordan Differently  
Audit date: **21 October 2026**, Asia/Amman. Application: http://127.0.0.1:4184. Existing Supabase project: dkhwwvoplhfjccvjegty.

**Documentation-only audit. No React, CSS, animation, dependencies, Auth settings, database, Storage, publication or permission changes were made. Phase 07 was not started.**

The complete machine-readable inventory is [BUTTON_INVENTORY.csv](BUTTON_INVENTORY.csv). IDs below match that UTF-8 CSV. Each entry includes all requested fields there; the expandable records below explain the interaction and its evidence, rather than listing labels alone.

## 1 — Executive Summary

### Counting rules and results

- **467 distinct audited control/behavior variants** have unique IDs. These are inventory definitions, not 467 unique handler functions and not 467 simultaneous buttons. Option values, route targets, Auth submit modes and guest-versus-account persistence are separated when behavior materially differs.
- The scan read **150 source/resource/style files**, parsed **124 JS/JSX files**, and found **350 JSX candidates**. **38** candidates were containers/focus targets, duplicate rendering primitives, composite wrappers, or unreachable code. **312 actionable source sites** remain. Known data-driven choices, hidden dynamic image-button syntax, generated map/chart controls and important behavioral branches expand these into the 467 records.
- Shared Button/Field primitives are not counted again merely because a call site renders through them. A dynamic destination/photo/category row is a template, not a claim that an unlimited future collection has a fixed number of controls.
- Four fresh browser snapshots contained **126 layout-rendered occurrences** in total: 59 desktop English Explore, 17 desktop Arabic Login, 17 mobile English Login and 33 mobile Arabic Explore. This sum intentionally repeats shared Navbar controls between snapshots. Layout boxes, including offscreen and disabled controls, were counted; hidden/inert controls were excluded. Other open dialogs/filters, data sizes and permissions change the number, so there is no honest fixed whole-application rendered-occurrence total.

| Area | Inventory variants | Working | Partial | Broken | Unverified |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Public Website | 159 | 48 | 6 | 1 | 104 |
| Authentication & Account | 52 | 6 | 0 | 0 | 46 |
| Admin Dashboard | 256 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 256 |
| **Total** | **467** | **54** | **6** | **1** | **406** |

**Status meaning:** WORKING is limited to the explicitly recorded genuine guest browser effect. PARTIAL means a missing or inconsistent intended behavior/feedback was established. BROKEN means a reproducible functional failure in the recorded state. UNVERIFIED is not a failure: protected account/Admin actions, untriggered error branches, conditional controls and external destinations were inspected but not exercised end to end. All **256 Admin variants** remain unverified as authenticated actions; the signed-out guard is a separate browser observation. No protected write is marked working because of a simulated test.

### Main findings

1. **Fix hit targets before adding animations.** Desktop Near You sorting can be covered by compact destination links/buttons, even with only its own panel open. Ordinary pointer activation is blocked; keyboard implementation exists. More filters and Near You also allow overlapping open panels.
2. **Correct save feedback first.** My Discoveries retains “Updating your saved places...” after removal. Discovery Result announces that saves disappear on refresh, although guest persistence was verified in localStorage. Account saving is implemented but was not written to during this audit.
3. **Do not animate unavailable features as if implemented.** Navbar Search is deliberately disabled; Visited tracking is an explicit placeholder. Google OAuth is conditional and currently hidden: the actual public Auth settings reported google=false, email=true, mailer_autoconfirm=false.
4. **Existing motion is substantial, but fragmented.** Seventeen source modules import Motion. Shared Button/ButtonLink already lift/press; Admin uses a separate CSS family, markers/cameras have their own feedback, and many text links/disclosures have no dedicated press or opening transition.
5. **Guard unsaved editing before visual changes.** Source inspection shows global Admin refresh increments revision and changes keyed editor identity. Advanced unsaved form state has no explicit in-app refresh-discard confirmation. This is a source-confirmed risk requiring a future authenticated, isolated test, not a claimed live data-loss reproduction.

### Actual route/component coverage

Public routes: /, /preferences, /explore, /map, /surprise-me, /discovery-result, /places/:slug, /my-discoveries, /profile, /auth, /auth/callback, and the wildcard not-found route. /login, /register and /forgot-password redirect to the corresponding unified Auth mode while preserving a safe return target. Auth query modes are login, register, recovery, reset and confirmation; reset without verified recovery proof shows its guarded error state.

Admin is dispatched inside /admin/*: overview, places, places/new, places/:id (Quick Edit), places/:id?advanced=1, categories, media, translations, publishing, audit, acceptance and development-only content-completion. #media/#review and ?preview=1 are states of the existing editor, not new standalone pages. /admin/accept-invite and /admin/recovery use the separate Admin callback. /admin/login is the existing signed-out gate; unknown permitted Admin sections fall back to Overview rather than a separate Admin 404.

The public Navbar uses the same navigation in a responsive two-row mobile arrangement; there is no separate public hamburger control. There is **no implemented theme switcher and no public footer component**. The Admin footer is noninteractive text. Badges, information-card icons, decorative hero images, compass art, progress/badge illustrations and noninteractive card wrappers were excluded. A compact destination card uses a stretched title anchor; its image is a div. Noncompact cards use a dynamic ImageControl button for preview. Featured cards lift on hover but only their live title link navigates; their decorative image is not an invented button.

Unrouted source files found by import tracing: ShellPage.jsx, PlaceInfoTile.jsx, the old DemoDiscoveriesProvider.jsx, discovery/formValidation.js and discovery/sample.js. The live shared favorite hook resolves through UserAccountProvider; the obsolete demo provider must not be mistaken for current saving behavior.

### Reading labels and evidence

Arabic/English labels come from authored JSX, ar-JO resources, translation patterns, or runtime destination/category values. “Runtime” placeholders are deliberate, not invented translations. “No exact mapping for audit alias” distinguishes an explanatory audit name from a literal visible UI string; it is not automatically a localization defect. The language button literally displays العربية in English mode and English in Arabic mode. Provider/licence names remain proper names. Native map/dialog dismissal surfaces and chart tooltips have no separate visible button label.

## 3 — Authentication and Account Button Inventory

The public explorer and Admin clients/session stores remain separate. Auth mode switches and safe invalid-field validation were genuinely observed without remote submission. Registration, real email delivery, valid recovery/reset, Google OAuth, authenticated profile edits, owner saved-place writes and cross-device preference synchronization are not current acceptance passes. Earlier owner confirmation of recovery/sign-in is historical evidence, not a new test of every branch. The profile, account-conflict, avatar, email-change and logout operations below remain accurately scoped.

## 5 — Functional Problems

### Reproduced defects and incomplete features

| ID | Severity / scope | Finding | Verified evidence / required follow-up |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| UJ-I-0014 | PARTIAL | Favorite {{place.name}} | Actual aria-pressed true; adjacent sr-only result announcement said Temporarily saved for this visit. Cleared on refresh; nothing saved to an account. Guest localStorage persistence was independently verified, so the announcement is stale. |
| UJ-I-0035 | PARTIAL | Remove {{place.name}} from saved places | Actual guest localStorage save/remove was checked; favorite persisted after reload. Removal worked but completion feedback remained Updating your saved places... . No account data written. |
| UJ-I-0044 | PARTIAL | Search (coming later) | Actual disabled=true plus source Search (coming later); intentional unavailable feature with no handler. |
| UJ-I-0045 | PARTIAL | More filters | Native disclosure opens, but actual desktop panel/card hit-test obstruction reproduced; independent panels can overlap. |
| UJ-I-0062 | PARTIAL | Near You / Near You · active | Native disclosure opens, but actual desktop panel/card hit-test obstruction reproduced; independent panels can overlap. |
| UJ-I-0066 | BROKEN | Nearest first when location is active | Live 1366×768 split view: after panel scroll, checkbox rect x124/y679/w20/h20, elementFromPoint centre returned Dana Biosphere Reserve stretched link; another attempt hit a locate button. Normal pointer activation repeatedly intercepted. |
| UJ-I-0382 | PARTIAL | Visited | Real tab activation and ArrowLeft selection worked. Visited explicitly has no tracking and renders a placeholder; Saved renders/removes guest saves. |

**Near You reproduction:** at 1366×768, open live Explore in split/map view, open Near You, and scroll its panel to the nearest-first checkbox. The checkbox rectangle was x=124, y=679, width=20, height=20. Hit-testing its centre returned the Dana Biosphere Reserve stretched destination anchor; another run returned a Locate destination button. Normal pointer activation was repeatedly intercepted after panel scrolling. Closing More filters did not remove the problem. Source shows the panel inside .explore-controls (stacking z-index 1), .explore-location-tools (5) and panel (10), alongside transformed compact cards/stretched links; increasing a child z-index alone must not be assumed sufficient. This is a documented stacking/hit-target failure in this state, not a claim that all location features are broken. GPS permission was not requested during this audit.

**Saved-place feedback:** the actual guest favorite changed aria-pressed and persisted across reload. My Discoveries removal updated the collection, but its local feedback stayed “Updating your saved places...” because remove() sets that message without a completion replacement. DiscoveryResultContent.jsx:28 still announces “Temporarily saved for this visit. Cleared on refresh; nothing saved to an account.” after a save; the current UserAccountProvider persists guest saves to localStorage and implements owner account synchronization. Correct the announcement before layering success motion onto it. The CSV separates guest and authenticated branches so a guest pass cannot imply an account API pass.

### Source-confirmed risks / UX gaps, not claimed live protected failures

- **Global Admin refresh may discard editor state.** AdminApp.jsx:36 invalidates data and increments revision. Workspace keys editor identity with loaded.key (which includes revision). Advanced fields are component state without its own in-app refresh discard prompt. Quick Edit attempts private autosave; that does not establish that every refresh/concurrency scenario is safe. Retest with an isolated Admin draft before approving a global refresh animation.
- **Pending/read feedback is inconsistent.** Most Admin writes use a shared busy wrapper and toast/error, but native text buttons, read pagination/filtering and account preference refresh vary. A spinner or checkmark must not imply that an unexecuted write succeeded. Quick save can intentionally save privately rather than apply a public change; keep that distinction visible.
- **Two independent panels can stay open.** Near You and More filters do not coordinate open state or implement Escape/outside-click dismissal. This compounds the measured hit-target problem. PreferenceField and account menus already provide more explicit Escape behavior.
- **Disabled Search looks almost active.** SiteHeader.css rules keep disabled header buttons at opacity 1, while its name/title says coming later. It has no handler. Preserve honest unavailable semantics until the feature is deliberately implemented.
- **Visited and badge/progress artwork are not activity features.** The tab navigation itself works, but tracking/earned achievements are not implemented. Do not recommend celebratory animations that suggest real visits or rewards.
- **Some cards advertise motion beyond their clickable region.** Featured-card wrapper hover lifts while only its live title navigates; its photo is not a preview trigger. Compact destination cards intentionally use a stretched link, with sibling favorite/locate buttons above it. Preserve those distinct hit areas and avoid a global card onClick.
- **Missing-data actions are deliberately unavailable.** Directions disable without valid coordinates; demo cost/group filters disable; no numeric price becomes free. These guarded controls are not classified broken merely for being disabled. Those unavailable branches remain source-only unless evidence explicitly says otherwise.
- **Stale operational copy exists in Admin.** Acceptance/content-completion descriptions still refer to the “six original drafts” and old public visibility expectations, while current live Explore displayed six published records. This audit changes neither records nor copy, and does not run those utilities. Publishing evidence packages have freshness checks and must not be assumed current.
- **Not-found source copy is demo-specific.** A missing live place can display wording about a local demo collection; recovery links still point to Explore/Home. This is copy inconsistency, not a proven wrong navigation target.
- **Frontend-validation focus differs.** Surprise Me explicitly focuses the first invalid field; Preferences opens its exact-limits disclosure but does not explicitly focus the first invalid input. Preserve accessible error association before animating validation.
- **Provider availability is a configuration condition.** Google Auth is implemented conditionally, currently hidden because public settings report disabled. No credentials/provider setup was changed and no OAuth journey was claimed.

## 6 — Current Animation Audit

### Source-derived inventory coverage

These categories partition the **467 inventory variants**, not unique browser animation timelines. Parent/content animation is explicitly distinguished from feedback on the control itself.

| Current family | Inventory variants |
| --- | ---: |
| Category press Motion + CSS | 8 |
| Shared Button/ButtonLink Motion | 32 |
| Card ancestor Motion (not independent control motion) | 11 |
| Native/static or no dedicated control motion | 95 |
| Gallery content fade (not independent control motion) | 5 |
| Map control/camera feedback | 32 |
| Admin CSS feedback | 256 |
| Auth parent choreography (not independent control motion) | 11 |
| Preference choice Motion + CSS | 17 |

Seventeen source modules import Motion for React. Existing shared Button and ButtonLink use hover y=-2, press scale=.98 and 160ms; disabled Button suppresses motion. CategoryFilter adds scale=.96 with no explicit Motion timing, plus CSS 160ms selected color. PreferenceChoice uses hover/press with Motion defaults and 180ms surface shadow. These defaults are not yet one consistent token system.

DestinationCard/SavedPlaceCard/FeaturedCard hover-lift by 1–4px over 180–200ms. Compact cards add 160ms shadow transitions. Favorite state is a background/dot, not a heart-fill animation; use the actual bookmark/favorite artwork and existing branding rather than inventing a new icon identity. Reveal ancestors enter with opacity/y12 over 400ms and per-item delays; do not count that as per-button feedback.

Admin CSS has a separate 180ms background/shadow/transform family, native icon/text/link overrides and 180–200ms modal/menu/toast entry. Sidebar width/content margin transitions run for 200ms and involve layout. Field border/shadow transitions are 180ms. Recharts bars animate 180ms with reduced-motion guard. Skeleton shimmer is 1.5s linear/infinite, loading-only; no need to add more persistent decoration.

Map control colors often change instantly. Destination markers scale to 1.09 with shadow over 180ms; selected ring is static. Camera durations are 250ms zoom, 400ms marker select, 500ms cluster, 600ms bounds reset and 700ms focused travel, reduced to 0 through existing guards. These spatial operations must remain separate from button feedback; never apply a global scale to the map canvas or its coordinate-placement transforms.

Authentication retains its intentional 620ms horizontal panels, 240ms form entry with 180ms delay, 140ms exit, 200ms welcome copy and 350ms initial shell entry. A 620ms branded panel transition is not an excessive duration for every button: button press should remain much shorter. The sizing refinement and current choreography are preserved.

### Accessibility, reduced motion and performance implications

- Global focus-visible outline is 3px; Admin uses terracotta, translation-review controls use an additional gold-toned outline. Preserve focus rings independently of hover/press.
- MotionConfig reducedMotion=user, component useReducedMotion and global/ Admin CSS overrides are present. **CSS marker hover still applies the spatial scale value instantly when durations are shortened**; eliminating duration is not the same as eliminating motion. Recommend an explicit reduced-motion/no-scale policy later.
- Native details use immediate open/close; no costly height animation exists there today. Avoid adding height:auto animation globally, which could jump surrounding content and obscure focus.
- Width/margin sidebar transitions and changing review-button border/padding can involve layout. Use transform/opacity for new feedback, but fix stacking first because a transformed ancestor creates a new stacking context.
- Box-shadow/background transitions are short but paint work; large repeating shadows, blur, multiple nested card/button transforms and many simultaneous marker pulses would add cost without improving the task.
- Header, text actions, external links and native disclosures do not all have a dedicated hover/press/loading treatment. This is **not** proof that they have no feedback: native focus, checked/selected/expanded states and parent motion are recorded separately.
- No current whole-application FPS, CPU or latency benchmark was performed for this documentation task. Browser observations verify interactions/DOM, not a claimed performance improvement.

Source anchors: [Button](../src/components/ui/Button.jsx), [ButtonLink](../src/components/ui/ButtonLink.jsx), [Reveal](../src/components/ui/Reveal.jsx), [map styles](../src/styles/maps.css), [Admin styles](../src/styles/admin.css), [Auth page](../src/pages/AuthPage.jsx), [global reduced motion](../src/styles/global.css), [translation-review styling](../src/features/admin/translationReview.css).

## 7 — Recommended Global Micro-interaction System

**Recommendation: extend the existing primitives, do not install a new library or attach a global document click animator.** Keep semantic native button/anchor/input elements, their refs, handlers, form behavior, disabled guards, RLS/Auth boundaries and current route architecture intact. Global styling must not make decorative content clickable.

A future implementation can expose small semantic variants through the existing Button/ButtonLink and shared Admin styles: primary, secondary, navigation, icon, favorite, disclosure, submit, destructive and map-tool. Use shared CSS timing/easing tokens, logical RTL origins and an explicit opt-out for map controls/auth-panel choreography. Prefer CSS hover/focus/active; use existing Motion only for state transitions that already need it. Avoid duplicate CSS and Motion transforms on the same node or nested parent/child lifts.

| Type | Recommended future interaction | Duration / implementation | Priority | Performance risk | Reduced-motion alternative |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Primary CTA | <=2px hover lift and .98 press, no layout size change | Hover 140–160ms, press 100–120ms; reuse Button/ButtonLink | P1 | Low; avoid parent duplication | Instant color/pressed state |
| Secondary/outline | Background/border change, optional small press | 120–160ms CSS ease-out | P1 | Low; avoid animated border width | Instant color/border |
| Navigation/brand | Active underline/color, stable hit area | 120–160ms CSS pseudo-element scaleX with RTL-aware origin | P1 | Low; no route remount | Immediate active indicator + focus |
| Favorite/save toggle | Icon-only selected fill/pop after state changes; preserve rollback | 180–220ms CSS/existing Motion | P2 | Low icon-only, higher on every card | Static selected fill/aria-pressed |
| Card/marker selection | One selected ring and restrained hover; keep sibling actions separate | 140–180ms; no whole-map scale | P2 | Medium for large inventories; cluster remains | Static ring/outline |
| Map zoom/reset | Short tactile icon response, camera controlled separately | 100–140ms CSS | P2 | Low per tool | Immediate press/camera duration 0 |
| Dropdown/tab | Brief opacity/<=4px reveal; keyboard focus immediate | 120–160ms, native semantics/progressive CSS | P2 | Low after hit-target fixes | Instant expanded/selected state |
| Form/auth submit | Unified busy label, disabled state and truthful result | 120–160ms feedback; existing auth panel unchanged | P3 | Low; never add network timers | Text/status only |
| Upload/replace | Chosen-file highlight, actual pending status then completion | 120ms, progress only if measured | P4 | Low; preserve responsive image cache/quality | Uploading/Complete/Error text |
| Delete/review/publish | Confirm first, restrained pending/real outcome | 100–140ms press, no celebratory preapproval | P0 guard first, P4 visuals | Low; no delayed/repeated operation | Static confirmation/pending/error |
| Text field/select | Border/focus accent, preserve native picker and comfortable size | 100–140ms CSS, no per-keystroke motion | P3 | Low | Instant focus/checked state |

Async feedback must reflect the actual operation: guest local save, optimistic account save with rollback, private autosave, valid public application, translation-only review and publication are different outcomes. Do not show a “published” checkmark for a private working draft or a licence-approved animation merely because a File was selected. Keep role=status/alert announcements accurate and nonduplicated.

Use hover effects only for fine pointers where appropriate, retain visible keyboard focus, and keep disabled/aria-disabled genuinely nonactivating. Do not persist animation state, user secrets or precise location. No additional Supabase query should be required for a hover, press, menu or language animation.

## 8 — Prioritized Future Implementation Plan

**P0 — functional prerequisites before visual rollout:** fix the reproduced Near You/card stacking and pointer interception; coordinate panels/close behavior; replace stale save announcements/completion text; verify the global Admin refresh against unsaved isolated edits. Preserve disabled Search and honest Visited placeholder until their separate feature scopes are approved. Do not change any of these during this audit.

1. **Priority 1 — core navigation and primary CTAs.** Consolidate the existing Button/ButtonLink timing tokens and navigation indicators, protect focus/disabled behavior, avoid duplicate parent/child transforms. Validate public Navbar/landing at desktop/mobile and RTL.
2. **Priority 2 — cards, favorites and maps.** Use one icon/selection treatment, preserve favorite-versus-navigation hit areas and guest/account failure rollback. Audit coordinate maps and clusters with a realistic larger fixture; preserve map instance/camera behavior and required attribution.
3. **Priority 3 — forms and authentication.** Unify pending/error/success presentation without modifying Auth, PKCE, storage/session restoration or panel timing. Fix first-invalid-field focus differences; test reduced motion and hidden-form inert behavior. Keep profile draft/guest preference conflicts explicit.
4. **Priority 4 — Admin actions and secondary controls.** Apply existing tokens to Admin button/icon/text actions and lazy sections. Verify protected flows with an authorized session and isolated data after approval; never animate as a substitute for rights, translation, publication or destructive-action confirmation.

Future acceptance should measure the interaction itself, not just screenshot appearance: keyboard activation, no wrong navigation, no false-success announcements, no input loss, no hover-generated fetches, no map remount from ordinary tab return, no large layout shifts, and zero ordinary-user/Admin permission crossover.

External map credits were read directly from actual DOM; all seven had an empty target attribute and follow the same browser tab. Their external pages were not followed.

### Evidence boundaries and test procedure

The source crawl included native buttons/anchors/inputs/selects/textareas/summaries, React Router links, custom Button/Field/Preference components, event handlers, dynamic ImageControl, generated Popup/NavigationControl/attribution links and Recharts keyboard/hover tooltips. It found 117 authored onClick attributes, 100 onChange, 12 onSubmit and 6 onKeyDown, plus close/cancel/drag/custom callbacks. Form containers/keyboard hosts were associated with their actual controls instead of counted as a second button.

Initial automated probes that sampled exit animations immediately, attempted to click behind an already-open modal, waited for hidden mobile list cards to be visible, or waited for a full document load after SPA navigation were not used as product failures. Controls were re-observed with appropriate settled state/keyboard and route checks. The Near You issue remained reproducible with separate hit-testing and normal pointer interception after scrolling, so it was retained as a functional finding. Some longer automation batches timed out; incomplete observations are not promoted to passes.

No new fixture success was represented as genuine Auth/Admin acceptance. Existing test scripts and prior validation reports were read as context; they were **not re-run**, because many create JSON/screenshots or isolated test records and this task permits only the two report files. Oxlint/build were also not run: no application code changed, and a build would write outside the permitted documentation scope. No performance speedup is claimed.

### Source preservation and exclusions

The final read-only source hash comparison covered all 150 inspected src files and matched the pre-document-write snapshot. Only the requested Markdown and CSV were created/updated. No dependency install, migration, Supabase configuration call, Storage object modification or original connection replacement was performed.

The index is an internal source-scan reference, not an inventory ID. Important excluded render primitives are expanded via the call sites/options in CSV. Five concrete Surprise Me selects use the shared PreferenceField implementation; its interest summary is a separate control. CoordinatePicker wrapper callbacks map to the actual picker canvas/pin. Dynamic ImageControl and library-created controls are added explicitly. Backend-only functions such as publishLocalized, repository aliases and callback consumers are dependencies, not invented independent buttons unless a real rendered trigger exists.

## 10 — Final Recommendations

**Approve a small functional-feedback correction pass before a global animation pass.** First address Near You hit targets, stale save announcements and explicit pending/completion language, then validate unsaved Admin refresh with isolated authorized editing. Next consolidate the existing primitives/tokens in the stated priorities, preserving the current brand, auth sliding panels, RTL, image delivery and map architecture.

The audit does not authorize or implement those changes. Protected account/Admin operations still need separately controlled acceptance using an available authorized session; source inspection alone cannot establish hosted success. Avoid changing the disabled Search, unfinished Visited feature or conditional Google configuration as part of a purely visual rollout.

**Deliverables:** [Markdown report](COMPLETE_BUTTON_INTERACTION_AUDIT.md) and [CSV inventory](BUTTON_INVENTORY.csv). Both use the same 467 IDs. The application remains unchanged; wait for the administrator’s review before implementing animations or starting another phase.
